name: Sirius
notes: Brightest star in the night sky; in Canis Major

name: Canopus
notes: Second brightest; southern sky; in Carina

name: Rigil Kentaurus
notes: Nearest star system to Sun; southern; in Centaurus

name: Arcturus
notes: Brightest star in northern hemisphere; in Boötes

name: Vega
notes: Keystone of Summer Triangle; in Lyra

name: Capella
notes: Bright yellow giant; in Auriga

name: Rigel
notes: Blue supergiant; lower-right of Orion

name: Procyon
notes: Brightest in Canis Minor; Winter Triangle

name: Achernar
notes: Bright blue star; far southern; end of Eridanus

name: Betelgeuse
notes: Red supergiant; upper-left of Orion; variable

name: Hadar
notes: Southern; near Alpha Centauri

name: Acrux
notes: Southern Cross; far southern sky

name: Altair
notes: Summer Triangle; spins very fast; in Aquila

name: Aldebaran
notes: Red giant; eye of Taurus; V-shaped Hyades cluster

name: Antares
notes: Red supergiant; heart of Scorpius; summer sky

name: Spica
notes: Brightest in Virgo; blue-white binary

name: Pollux
notes: Brighter twin of Gemini; orange giant

name: Fomalhaut
notes: Bright isolated star in southern Piscis Austrinus

name: Deneb
notes: Summer Triangle; tail of Cygnus; distant supergiant

name: Mimosa
notes: Southern Cross; second brightest in Crux

name: Regulus
notes: Brightest in Leo; almost on the ecliptic

name: Adhara
notes: Brightest in Canis Major after Sirius

name: Castor
notes: Twin of Gemini; actually a sextuple star system

name: Shaula
notes: Near tip of Scorpius tail; summer sky

name: Bellatrix
notes: Upper-right shoulder of Orion
